content.title: Dana White Promises Free UFC White House Tickets, But Joe Rogan Voices Concerns
content.text: The UFC CEO Dana White has confirmed that a staggering 85,000 free tickets will be given away for the UFC's historic "Freedom 250" event at the White House on June 14.White revealed that the free admission will grant fans access to the Ellipse, a park directly across from the White House’s South Lawn, where the fights will be shown on massive screens. The landmark event will take place on the South Lawn to celebrate 250 years of the United States, coinciding with President Donald Trump's 80th birthday.AdvertisementDonald Trump and Dana WhiteEd Mulholland-GettyImages (Ed Mulholland-GettyImages)While the main card will feature a very limited audience of 3,000 to 5,000 VIPs on the actual lawn, the surrounding area will host tens of thousands of passionate fans.White Says Tickets Will be "Free"He spoke to Brendan Fitzgerald and Michael Bisping on Thursday, March 12, about details of the “Freedom 250” event, as well as other upcoming events (via UFC on YouTube):"We're gonna be ticketing 85,000 people in the Ellipse, and the tickets are free, and we'll announce how we're gonna be giving them away soon," White stated.AdvertisementHe added that the Ellipse will be transformed into a massive festival ground, telling fans, "There's gonna be music. Bands are gonna be playing, and you can actually sit in the park and watch the fight on the screens.”White encouraged fans to start planning their trips immediately, emphasizing the unique nature of the experience."You should plan on going to Washington DC for this event," he urged fans, noting that the press conference will also be held at a historic location, the Lincoln Memorial.AdvertisementThe UFC is planning a full week of activations throughout the city to complement the fight card.Who is Fighting on the “Freedom 250” UFC Card?The main event for "UFC: Freedom 250" will see Ilia Topuria defend his lightweight belt against interim champion Justin Gaethje.Ilia TopuriaGetty Images (Getty Images)In the co-main event, Alex Pereira will attempt to become the UFC's first three-weight champion when he faces Ciryl Gane for the interim heavyweight title.Alex Pereira during his walkout at UFC 307Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images (Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images)Other high-profile bouts on the card include Sean O'Malley vs. Aiemann Zahabi and Michael Chandler vs. Mauricio Ruffy.AdvertisementThe event will also feature Bo Nickal, Kyle Daukaus, Diego Lopes, and Steve Garcia, with six of the 12 participants representing the United States.Joe Rogan Expresses ConcernsSecurity for the June 14 event is expected to be extraordinarily tight given the venue and global context. Joe Rogan addressed security concerns on his podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, this week (clip via Championship Rounds on X):"It's going to be very high security and high stress, and weird to have a fight at the White House in the middle of a f— war," Rogan said, referencing the ongoing conflict with Iran.AdvertisementHe expressed hope that the geopolitical situation would stabilize by June but admitted he wasn't confident that would be the case.Despite these challenges, White remains focused on delivering an unforgettable experience for the fans who make the trip. He assured that those in the Ellipse will have a clear view of the unique setup, with the White House serving as an iconic backdrop."You'll actually see the whole setup. It's right there," White explained. "It will be a very unique, cool experience for fight fans."AdvertisementThis story was originally published by Athlon Sports on Mar 13, 2026, where it first appeared in the MMA section.
